summary: Gridley sits in the flat, wide-open Sacramento Valley about 60 miles north of Sacramento, surrounded by rice fields and olive orchards — and that agricultural setting is more than scenery, because rice milling and olive oil production are genuine local employers alongside healthcare and public-sector jobs in a town of barely 7,400 people packed into just 2.2 square miles. That density — over 3,300 per square mile — is surprisingly urban for a place with open-sky farm horizons in every direction, and it means the compact street grid is genuinely walkable between its small downtown, schools, and parks without needing a car for every errand. At a median home price of roughly $298,000 against a median household income near $58,000, the price-to-income ratio lands around 5.1 — tight but not crushing compared to coastal California, though a median rent of $1,127 still absorbs nearly a quarter of gross monthly income. Summers are emphatic: average daily highs push well into the 90s with 9-plus hours of sunshine, while winter nights dip into the 30s under tule fog that blankets the valley floor for weeks. The graduation rate across Gridley's six schools sits at a solid 92.7%, though math proficiency scores trail state benchmarks significantly at 37 points below standard. Gridley is, at its core, a compact agricultural service town offering Sacramento Valley affordability — with the trade-off that switching employers without a commute means a very short list of options.
